newsitem.title: USA: Farmland to build $250 mln Kansas ammonia plant.
newsitem.headline: Farmland to build $250 mln Kansas ammonia plant.

text.p: Farmland Industries Inc plans to build a $250 million ammonia plant at its Coffeyville, Kansas oil refining facility pending receipt of financing, the company's chief operating officer said.
He said the two-year, $250 million project will apply gasification technolgy to the refinery's petroleum coke stream to make hydrogen, a feedstock of ammonia-based fertilizer.

"What we're doing is taking a waste product (in the coke) and making a fertilizer plant," said Bob Honse, COO of Farmland, a cooperative owned by farmers and ranchers. "We should have financing done by summer," he said.

He said the 1,100 ton-per-day plant will have the side effect of boosting the refinery's fluid catalytic cracking capacity, now rated at about 28,000 barrels per day by creating a new flow of oxygen as a by-product.
He said it too early to estimate by how much the cat cracker's output might be boosted since it was now impossible to estimate the magnitude of the upcoming oxygen stream.
Regarding other potential expansions of the refinery's catalytic reforming, coking and hydrotreating capacity, Honse said those projects were all on the "backburner."
"I would characterize all those projects as way back on the backburner. Right now we're trying to identify bottlenecks," he said.
Farmland's Coffeyville refinery now has crude distillation capacity of about 110,000 bpd.
((-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk, 1 212 859 1633))
